Craig Tribal Association

Craig Tribal Association is a local Tribal government connected with the Tlingit and Haida communities of Craig. This guide pairs a dated federal history with a Native corporation’s account of a longstanding fishing place and public connections to Elder oral histories.

The two sources offer different institutional perspectives on the same community. Read source annotations for selected pages, dates, perspective and access limits. These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

A fishing place and a collective government

The BIA’s 2017 account describes Craig as an earlier herring-roe and fish-camp site associated with Tlingit Shangukeidi and Haida Kaigani people. It records the Association’s 1938 organization and connects the cannery settlement with later community-building work. This dated institutional history provides a starting point for exploring the local government’s history.

Read the sources [1] Bureau of Indian Affairs / Office of Public Affairs

02

Place and Elder oral-history connections

Sealaska’s community page reproduces a short historical passage credited to the Shaan-Seet website. It connects a longstanding herring fishing place near Craig with cultural significance and oral histories passed down by Elders of Craig, Klawock and Hydaburg. The passage introduces a public route toward community-directed historical reading; the individual narratives and underlying records have not been reviewed here.

Read the sources [2] Sealaska / MySealaska

03

Following different local institutions

The same page names Craig Tribal Association under its tribal-government heading and Shaan-Seet, Inc. under its ANCSA village-corporation heading. Keeping these institutions distinct helps readers follow government and corporate sources about the community. The source’s historical passage is credited to the corporation, while the BIA account supplies the selected government history.

Read the sources [2] Sealaska / MySealaska [1] Bureau of Indian Affairs / Office of Public Affairs

Interior Approves Craig Tribal Association’s Land-into-Trust Application ↗

Publication: 2017-01-13

A dated federal account connects the Association’s government history with the earlier herring and fishing camp at Craig.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual two-page PDF: header/date and historical community paragraphs on PDF pages 1–2; selected 1938 organization, earlier fishing camp, 1908 cannery and later community-building context.

Review recorded: November 2, 2026

Access note: Normal validating terminal request returned HTTP 200 and a PDF; selected text was read. The dated announcement is used for historical context. Current title, jurisdiction, gaming, legal advice, later administrative outcomes, legal quotations, acreage, aggregate figures and underlying cited records are excluded.

Sháan Séet (Craig) ↗

Publication: Undated public community page; footer copyright year is not a publication date

A short community account links a longstanding herring fishing place with oral histories passed down by Elders of Craig, Klawock and Hydaburg. The page separately identifies Craig Tribal Association and the ANCSA village corporation. It credits the historical passage to Shaan-Seet.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual main body, reader lines 43–45: the publicly stated relationship between a longstanding herring fishery, cultural significance and Elder oral histories. Separate institution headings and names at lines 46–68. Specific archaeological features and precise site locations are excluded. The linked Shaan-Seet website and underlying oral histories were not opened and do not count as separate reviewed works.

Review recorded: November 2, 2026

Access note: Exact URL read successfully through the normal public web reader during correction review. This is a regional Native corporation page reproducing a credited village-corporation passage, not a new statement authored by the tribal government. No individual oral narratives, archaeology inventory, current figures, or precise resource locations are reproduced.

https://www.mysealaska.com/Communities/Craig
